The idea is that the server's wage is lower, and tips make up a significant part of their income. So, tipping is more than just a courtesy; it's an economic necessity for many servers. Now, in this scenario, the man usually gives a large tip, which is commendable. But this time, he didn't because he didn't like the waitress's hair color. That seems problematic. Also, considering the economic aspect, if a server relies on tips for their income, not tipping adequately because of a personal dislike could have a negative impact on their earnings. It's not fair to penalize someone economically for something as trivial as their hair color. I should also think about the broader implications. It's expected that customers will tip regardless of their personal feelings about the server's appearance. In conclusion, not tipping because of the waitress's hair color seems wrong because it's based on personal bias rather than the quality of service.
